utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good morning. I'm afraid Judge Parker is unable to sit today as well, but we are certain that he will be able to join us tomorrow. So for today it will still be Judge Thelin and myself conducting the hearing. Good morning, Mr. Vojnovic. May I remind you of the affirmation you took yesterday which is still applicable. Now we are going to continue with the cross-examination. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just to finish what we began yesterday. If I were to tell you that Captain Radic had to go into coordinated action with his unit with two detachments of the Territorial Defence and with your 3rd Battalion, would he be able to do something like that of his own accord or would there have to be a decision on something like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He couldn't do it of his own accord. He couldn't choose who to go into coordinated action with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But based on what could he do something like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of an order by the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've already stated that you attended the daily briefings at the command post of OG South in Negoslavci. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that at those meetings Mrksic was also present with his staff. That's what you told the Tribunal investigators.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who comprised this staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the staff comprised the Chief of Staff, some of the operations organ, people in the staff, the security chief, the assistant, and the most serious senior officers from the OG South command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is that the main place where the command of the Vukovar operation was conducted from?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: On the critical day when you went for the regular briefing on the 20th of November, 1991, could you please list all the officers of yours who remained at Ovcara at that time.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that those who were at Ovcara on that day, on the 20th, other than me, were the following people: Vezmarovic -- I'm not mentioning the name of the person who was in the Ovcara sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You mean the local commander of Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Him. Then, later, Captain Vukic and Captain Dacic also came. I don't know of any others.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Dragi Vukosavljevic there with some officers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he was there with Dacic and Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The military police company under the command of Vezmarovic numbered about 30 soldiers. You said that to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was a platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Then on transcript page 8807, line 25, you said that a military police company is comprised of a military police platoon and a traffic police platoon.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: For the Prosecution, this is page 8827, line 25. You said that the military police platoon numbered between 25 and 30 and the traffic police had two detachments, numbering from 15 to 16 soldiers. Is that correct? If we add that up, doesn't that come to about 40 soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If we added the 16 soldiers who came with Vukic, does that mean that then there were about 50 soldiers at a certain point together with Vezmarovic's company?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the traffic platoon was not at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the traffic police was not at Ovcara, the traffic police detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard such information other than now from you that the traffic platoon was at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that Vezmarovic said that when he came to the command post he heard that his company of the military police was engaged at Ovcara, that means that if the military police company was engaged there, the traffic -- a platoon was engaged there as well.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he probably made a mistake. The traffic platoon was not engaged there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How would you recognise members of the traffic platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had slightly different equipment. They had white sleeves and they had the traffic bats, and they also had batons and handcuffs and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: The location of the Ovcara hangar as a location where the prisoners would be detained, is that something that was chosen by Vezmarovic together with you? I think we talked about that a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at that facility at Ovcara. I don't remember specifically, but I know that this building was meant to be used in the event that there were any prisoners of war, and it was supposed to be used for other purposes, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that as the commander of the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I planned that or someone else allocated that facility for that. But the facility was there, it was the only one, there were no other buildings available.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you felt it was the most suitable building?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That means that you allocated that as the future prison.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't really say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Based on your statement, we see that when you came to Ovcara you found Vezmarovic already there - is that correct? - with the members of the military police company?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think that Vezmarovic came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We are going to establish that now slowly. You said there were a lot of people there wearing white cross belts. Does that mean that these were members of the military police company?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't mean that. Somebody could have gotten white cross belts in some other way and could have worn it without being a member of the military police. In any case, white belts are an indication of membership of the military police. I don't know if any of the Territorial Defence members had white belts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Your military police company commander said that when he came to Ovcara, he, threw out all the military members and only his military police company remained behind and they were wearing white cross belts. So if you saw people with white cross belts in the hangar it is logical that these would be members of the military police company who belonged to your 80th Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right, very well. Thank you. Now, let's go back now to the time when you were there, because several times you said you spent from 20 to 30 minutes there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that you stopped by at the hangar on your way from Sotin, in your statement, and I think my colleague Vasic gave you that statement and I can give it to you to look over.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is correct; I stopped off at the hangar on my way from Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said there in a statement you gave to the security organs of the 12th of November --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the date and the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that there were from 20 to 30 members of paramilitary groups and Territorial Defence members at about 1200 hours you stopped off at the hangar in Sotin.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably that is what I stated, but I think that later I confirmed that. I think there were more than the number quoted there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please provide the Trial Chamber as well as the Prosecution with -- I thought that Mr. Vasic left everything to the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You gave a statement to the military court on the 28th of December, 1998. This is page 3, paragraph 2. The English version is page 3, paragraph 1. And there you also said that you arrived at 1700 hours and that you saw a person there making lists. You also said that you stayed there for about 20 minutes. There is another thing: You said that you didn't notice members of any regular units there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm missing one of the lenses from my glasses, but very well. I don't believe that Vezmarovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, you said that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I want to go back to the first part of what you said, that Vezmarovic threw out all the military personnel from the hangar, because he could not have thrown out all the TO members from the hangar, that's for sure. Maybe some of us or maybe he chased out some other people, but these people he could not have chased out of the hangar. I'm thinking of the TO members.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Well, then, let's finish up what you are commenting on yourself. So Vezmarovic said not only that he threw out members of the units belonging to the local commander of Ovcara, but he also threw out all the members of the Territorial Defence, and he also stated that at the time there were no officers or soldiers from the Guards Motorised Brigade at that location. What would your comment be now, because that was his statement?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that Major Vukasinovic was at the hangar --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We have already heard that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and around him were a group of persons wearing regular military uniforms. I don't know if these were senior officers or soldiers. I don't know. In any case, they were not our soldiers, and they were around him all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. What do you say about your statement that you provided to the security organs - that I read for you earlier - from the 12th of November, 1998, page 1, where you say: "I did not notice members of any regular units." You do not mention Vukasinovic there or those other soldiers. Vezmarovic doesn't mention them either.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Vukasinovic does not constitute a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. My colleagues asked you a little bit more about that so I'm not going to go into that so much. Were you at Ovcara that day at 1400 hours in passing and then after that at 1700 hours. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you wanted to visit your units in Sotin and then after that you wanted to visit your unit in Ovcara. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If you said that you wanted to see your commander and see your unit -- so isn't then your unit part of the 80th Motorised Brigade? You were saying something else yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not part of the 80th Brigade, but he is my officer who is temporarily out of that brigade. But I knew that in a few days he would come back to the brigade, so I couldn't just ignore him and pass by without checking to see what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that you passed by at 1400 hours on your way to Sotin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Sotin, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I stayed there -- I can't say exactly. I had lunch with them. Then I did some personal hygiene things for myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About two to two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When you arrived at Ovcara, how long did you make efforts on behalf of the prisoners there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very easy to be talking constantly about the time-line. I know the events, I know some details. I can say some things about Ovcara as a facility, about the Mitnica group, about the prisoners. So I cannot really say I was there for 20 minutes and then later you will say: Well, you said you were there for 30 minutes. So I'm not sure how many minutes I was there. I was there for as long as it took me to make sure that all the prisoners entered Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So let us go on. How much time did you need as long as the gauntlet was active and until all the prisoners entered?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say how much --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How much time did you need for that operation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really cannot tell how much time it took.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How much time did you spend in the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I spent about 30, up to 40, minutes in the hangar. I don't know myself, I'm not sure how long it was. Mostly it was, I think, about 30 minutes. I already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How much time did Vukic need after you called him to come to Ovcara? You can assess that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can estimate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To organise the troops and all of that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was 30 to 40 minutes, an hour at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that in contradiction with your statement, something that you repeated several times, that you spent a total of between 20 and 30 minutes inside the hangar at Ovcara? Would that not mean that you could not possibly have seen Vukic if 20 or 30 minutes later you left for Negoslavci?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I waited for Vukic, that's why I'm saying this. Don't hold me to a precise time-line. I'm telling you about what happened and how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sir, our task is to check if you're telling the truth. If there is a 20-minute discrepancy regarding your time in the hangar, then I have to check several things with other witnesses, because for all I know, you may have arrived at Ovcara at 1400 hours and that would seem to tie in perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to ask this one directly, I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were you at Ovcara from 1400 hours until your departure for the Negoslavci command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot really say that I was or that I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In the transcript of the trial, the Special Court for war crimes in Belgrade, dated the 24th of November, page 70 - the English reference is page 101 - you were asked the following question by the President of the Trial Chamber: "Were there any other units?" And you said: "No, no one." And after that, on page 70, you said: "No one. All I can say is I think there was a patrol of the traffic police in that task that was sent there to help with the traffic flow when those people were coming out of the hospital. Traffic patrol was requested to provide security." My question is: Your traffic patrol from the 80th Motorised Brigade, was it involved in any way with the captured persons coming out of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And yet I have just read out to you your own testimony from the Special Court in Belgrade. Is that true what you stated there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was indeed what I said, and yesterday I said I thought there was but there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was it that persuaded you that there wasn't?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just talked to people and it donned on me at some point that there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I suppose that one of those people you talked to must have been Vezmarovic, too, that you colluded with him to decide what your testimony would be, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never met Vezmarovic before any of the trials nor did I actually see him at any of the trials.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about the meeting in Kragujevac; did you see him there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw Vezmarovic in Kragujevac, when my daughter --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. My learned friend is posing a question to the witness. He is not giving him a chance to refer specifically to the issue. I have managed to locate the evidence that my learned friend is referring to. Initially I thought he had been submitting to the witness or asking the witness about what he saw at 2.00 when he was there. My understanding in relation to this section of the transcript relates to later -- later that day, in relation to the -- what I would call the gauntlet issue. I don't know if that is right or wrong. My learned friend moves so quickly, it's difficult to catch the documents, but it seems to be in relation to a different part of the day and a different issue, but perhaps I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Can you clarify that, Mr. Borovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's all crystal clear. There is a method that I'm using in my cross-examination by which I managed to obtain an answer from the witness. It may have been the case that he was at Ovcara that day from 1400 hours onwards. He said: Yes. The Prosecutor wishes to reprocess my question in order to obtain a different answer, but that is a very different kettle of fish, Your Honours. By now the witness understands that he's expected to change that answer, so ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never told you that I was at Ovcara throughout. You are trying to convince me that I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, should I do that again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm reading from the transcript on page 10, line 14, on my transcript and the witness answers: "I cannot say that I was or wasn't," so he hasn't answered yes to your question, according to what I see on the transcript. So maybe you can clarify this, please, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When I say that you were there throughout from 1400 hours onwards, that is until your departure for the command post in Negoslavci, inside the hangar, is there any possibility that you were there throughout?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer was -- I am not saying that I was there throughout and I wasn't there inside the hangar, if you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you allow for the possibility, if I may just jog your memory a little, that you were, after all, there throughout this whole time until you left for the command post in Negoslavci, from 1400 hours onwards. Do you allow for that possibility? Do you leave that possibility open that you were perhaps wrong on that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Negoslavci. I left for Negoslavci at about 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Before you left for Negoslavci. I am being crystal clear here. Please don't twist my question around.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not trying to do that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What would you say if I told you that you were at Ovcara from 1400 hours until you left for the command post in Negoslavci for your regular briefing, as you suggest, at about 1700 hours. You have just said that, haven't you? 1700 hours was the time of your departure for the command post in Negoslavci; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it obvious, then, that what you've been talking about for two days, that you had reached Ovcara a lot earlier than you originally suggested?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I finally came, I don't know if I was there all the time, but I know that I left at about 1700 hours for the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Vojnovic, I think we've managed, finally, to shed some light on this particular issue. If I told you that Dragi Vukosavljevic stated that he had been to Ovcara on your orders twice, would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what Dragi sent. I know that I sent him once and maybe he went yet another time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The second time around that you sent him to Ovcara, was that in order to convey your express orders to the military police to withdraw, to pull out?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if anyone asked you: Do you know who Novica Trifunovic from Kragujevac is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I heard that he was a soldier, but -- actually, excuse me, you probably mean an officer who was here recently. A man named Trifunovic testified here recently. I read about that in the newspapers. I'm not sure if that's the same person. Is he an officer or whatever?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, Novica Trifunovic from Kragujevac. That is the person I'm asking you about. Your commander of your military police company claims that he found Novica Trifunovic at Ovcara with soldiers and that he chucked them out of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I still don't know who Novica Trifunovic is, do I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about Jovan Novkovic, my apologies.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovan Novkovic, yes, yes, I know that person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that he was chucked out of the hangar by Vezmarovic on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You got pretty emotional yesterday when you explained to Mr. Vasic that the actual fact was you came across Ovcara and the hangar quite by accident and that is where the problem arose, and I'm asking you: Were not members of your 80th Motorised Brigade at the hangar even prior to your arrival? Would that not be true?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Didn't you say yesterday that the rope had been set up already at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just several soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you not say yesterday that the rope had already been set up by the time you arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The rope had already been set up by the time I arrived in the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that this rope was strung up by Vezmarovic, or at least, that's what he claims before this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea who set it up. All I know is when I came there it was there and it was up already.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What if I told you that this was Vezmarovic, that his military police company did that? Would it not seem to imply that they preceded you at Ovcara inside the hangar? I will do my best. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm that. I believed Vezmarovic to be on his way from Mitrovica to Negoslavci at the time. I didn't realise that he had been to the hangar previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about members of his company? Maybe they were the ones who put the rope up, the rope that you claim to have seen when you arrived.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been the local commander, whose name I shouldn't mention. Maybe there were two or three members of his group with white belts, but Vezmarovic was not there at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Furthermore, you stated that you had found there a regular JNA soldier who was drawing up some sort of list, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say he was a regular JNA soldier. He was a soldier who was seated there. He wasn't wearing a cap or anything. I'm not sure if he was JNA or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So who is it drawing up this list now? You were the commander there and you were protecting the prisoners and there was somebody drawing up lists of those prisoners. Did you check that or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't check who it was. I realised that there was a person in uniform seated at that table there, or desk, and drawing up lists. Now, as to who he was, from which unit, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to remove his hand from his mouth while speaking; we can't hear him properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that this member --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, can you remove your hand, because the interpreters can't hear you. Can you remove your hand from the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When talking about Vezmarovic, you have stated several times that you believed him to be on his way from Mitrovica back to Negoslavci and then on to Ovcara at the time, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What if I told you that he, while testifying before this International Court, clearly stated that he had been in Nijemci on that day and not in Mitrovica at all, but rather that it was from Nijemci that he eventually reached Negoslavci and, after that, Ovcara? Would that change anything about the way you feel about this particular incident?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not at all. To the best of my knowledge, whether he went from Mitrovica to Nijemci, I don't know. All in all, I'm saying he wasn't there, because why else would I be requesting assistance?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Let's leave this story alone for a while. You've been repeating this over and over for two days; he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that's the very same thing you're telling me about those two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about Nijemci.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Are you saying Vezmarovic isn't telling the truth when he says that he was in Nijemci on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not saying that. He may have left Mitrovica and drove through all the villages on the way in order to get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very fine. Thank you. Did you have any military of your own in Nijemci?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did, but I don't know exactly which one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind -- try to remember something specific, at least.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may be wrong: I think it was an engineers unit or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that you had a Campagnola with a piece of radio equipment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is this vehicle usually referred to as the small command staff vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that MS -- MKSK, is that the abbreviation normally used?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was this vehicle typically not at the disposal of battalion commanders only?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in terms of the establishment, but not always.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That means that some lower-ranking officers, company commanders and so on, could not have had it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the battalion commanders did not have all this equipment. In terms of establishment-wise, they were supposed to have all this equipment, but in actual fact they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about your military police company commander? He is a man within whose remit it is to guard the prisoners at Nijemci. We believe this was the case. Who could possibly have summoned him back for a new assignment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he came of his own accord, not having been summoned by anyone, he came to Negoslavci. At Negoslavci he heard at the brigade command that there was some sort of a mess at Ovcara. Without waiting, he just drove straight on to Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And he arrived without any of his military policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who he came with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think he came alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about his military police company? Were they perhaps at Ovcara already by the time he arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But you're saying that you do know. Firstly you say that you know that no one summoned him back and then I asked you: How do you know that no one summoned him back? Who told you that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What exactly did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That he had been told that Vezmarovic had already gone back. There was a mess at Ovcara, the commander was there, and he said something else. He wasted no time driving back and he drove straight back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Does that mean that when he got to Ovcara he found you there since the duty operations officer told him that the commander was already there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that now imply that you actually saw him arrive at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if I saw him arrive that very minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When was it, then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say. There were a lot of people milling around. There was a lot of coming and going. I do know that he was there, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who was in charge at this time? You know that he was at Ovcara. Who was in charge of establishing order, imposing discipline? Would that be the military police company commander or you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was Major Vukasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: For what, in charge of what?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the one who brought the prisoners there, he was the one who took them inside the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, sir. Who was it that pulled the rope up? Was that done by Major Vukasinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was Major Vukasinovic drawing up lists that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was Major Vukasinovic physically imposing order inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but that would have been his duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Was all of this not in fact not done by members of your 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It should have been --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the facts.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Facts about what?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All you're telling us about.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All these actions, all these steps, everything that I've just told you, what about the facts? Were all these things not done by members of -- your members of the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, pursuant to orders of Major Vukasinovic because he --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the speakers please kindly be asked not to speak at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who issued the order to the military police company, to Vukic, to the soldiers of the Ovcara local commander to carry out these tasks that I just asked you about? Was it you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you issue this order to all of them?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued an order to Vukic to report to Major Lukic [as interpreted] --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers pleased be asked to slow down, especially Mr. Borovic. It is very difficult to have an accurate transcript at this pace -- actually, it's impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see Major Vukasinovic ordering any kind of order or not in your presence?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were talking to some people there; we don't know who they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to repeat my question for the third time: Did you see Major Vukasinovic issuing an order members of the military police company, to the soldiers of the local commander of Ovcara, to you, or to anyone else, or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I -- no assignment was issued to Major Vukasinovic. I don't know whether he said anything to members of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we now briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Before we go into private, or even when we're in private, 21:3, I wonder whether in actual fact that is correct. There is a reference to a Major Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Moore. It should state Major Vukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Vukic is not a major, it's not Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: No, that can't be right either. Perhaps the question could be asked again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: When Vukic came at your summons, did you order him to do anything?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked us to move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: But we haven't dealt with the topic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can the witness explain to us, in case of an urgent necessity, how can he get in touch with the commander of the military police company when he needed him for an urgent assignment and he was not at the command post?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He was constantly in communication with the chief of security. Not with us, though, because he did not have a radio device installed in his vehicle. He didn't have an adequate vehicle. These were just provisional ill-equipped vehicles that were used at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did Vezmarovic drive a Campagnola?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not every Campagnola is equipped with a radio device.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if members of the military police company, together with the prisoners, arrived at Ovcara before you came?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where they were at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the military police company? I've explained that. I assumed they were somewhere between Sremska Mitrovica and Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You've also stated to the investigators of the OTP that you've learned from some local inhabitants at Negoslavci about the crime at Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend asked you a question yesterday and I wanted to follow-up. Did you have any physical contact with any investigator after the events, physical contact? Did you meet with any investigator?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean investigator from this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: No, from Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber how it came that you left Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slovenia: In an organised fashion, together with other units that were pulled out of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before this organised withdrawal, where were you in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in the Slovenska Bistrica garrison. I was commander of the 11th Partisan Brigade, and almost 100 per cent of our troops were Slovenians.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How did it come about that you left the garrison?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An order came from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you withdraw without any fighting from the garrison in Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please explain.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We secured our facilities that were attacked, and in the meantime an agreement was reached to have a cease-fire, and that's how we pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree with me that you haven't fired a single bullet before pulling out of Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree, and luckily so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did you fire a single bullet at Ovcara before you left and abandoned the prisoners at the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: If we are to go back to the Mitnica group now, did your military police company represent the main part of the security detail at Ovcara at the moment?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My officers who were securing the Mitnica group in the hangar were there together with some members of the military police company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The local commander of Ovcara, whose name we are not going to mention, was he the chief negotiator between the European Community and the Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Mitnica group was there?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. But I think he was assisting with the transport and security of civilians, of women and children, since he spoke English, and he offered -- he lent a hand there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he do that with your approval or his own?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were talking there, and he took part. He would explain to both sides what the requests were, what the opinion was, and he would pass on orders, and I believe it functioned well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Did he do that based on your approval?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were together. I didn't tell him: Please translate this for me. When they would ask questions, that was the first time that I realised that (redacted) spoke English, and this was a conversation we had. I didn't prohibit him from talking. Why would I?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You said that the task had been carried out successfully.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Concerning that particular task, how many members of the 80th Motorised Brigade were there together with officers?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know; not too many.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't say. There was an officer there, perhaps some of his associates, a group of soldiers, myself, some of our officers. I didn't need to remember that. It was done successfully, and I'm quite happy because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who commanded over the entire situation? Did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the most senior officer at the time there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And so you were in command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: You were. Did you say you were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know whether I commanded, but I was the most senior. Given that was a military situation, there was no need to have that clearly defined.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I asked you specifically who led the entire action. You said you were the most senior person there. I want to have a clear answer for the transcript: Were you the main person there and did you have the operation, did you follow it through?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know there were seven to nine buses of women and children.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: We know who was there. With your 80th Motorised Brigade, did -- were you in charge of the entire operation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We secured the people and they were taken away in an organised way, but I don't know exactly where.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the soldiers of your 80th Motorised Brigade carried out the entire operation of securing the prisoners, doing the negotiations by themselves, that it was only them there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question: Why didn't you repeat the same thing on the 20th of November with the same troops? You had done that on the 18th.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't the same operation; it was a completely different situation. On the first occasion I was the most senior. There were no officers from the superior command; in the latter example, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of November, did you ask for any assistance from where you were? You had your MKSK. Did you ask for a military police battalion to be sent or did you ask for any other unit that you may have deemed helpful? Did you ask that other members of the 80th Motorised Brigade come there because you could issue orders to them and you could ask for their assistance on the 20th of November from the location where you were?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the person who organised the whole thing and brought the people to the hangar could have done that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I will repeat the question: Did you ask for assistance --

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have no idea why the witness is being asked the question. He's given a perfectly clear answer. Why should the witness have to answer the question when he's answered so clearly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, excuse me. The witness did not provide a clear answer; he rather switched to another topic. My question was quite clear. Since he had a radio device in his MKSK, did he personally ask for some assistance, since he was on the location? As to who had the right to do that or not, that's another issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To repeat the question: Did you ask for any assistance from anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered already. I didn't ask for any assistance. The person who brought those people was the only who could have asked for some help. He was the one to bear the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Could you read out a paragraph -- but before that, I'll ask you this: Were there any proceedings instigated against you before the court in Belgrade for the incidents at Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time I've heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Were you ever interviewed as a suspect by any security organ or the police?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a statement given to the security organ. Maybe you had that in mind. I gave a statement to the security organ of the general staff and to the military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraph 42 - and that was the statement given to the OTP investigators - the same number in the B/C/S and in the English - that was in September and October of 2003 - you stated the following. I will read it out and please follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would kindly ask the usher to give that statement to you since I don't see it before you. We have an extra copy here; perhaps it could be passed on to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Please go to paragraph 42. In the first sentence of paragraph 42, does it state the following: "Considering my experience as JNA commander, and specifically my experience from Vukovar, I would not have handed over the evacuees/prisoners to anyone but the legitimate government." Is that what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: And then a few lines down does it state the following: "If Mrksic had ordered me to hand over the evacuees to the --"

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if my learned friend is going to read the passages, he must put the whole paragraph so the witness has an opportunity of seeing the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will continue, Your Honour, and perhaps my learned friend can clear things up in his redirect. We needn't go through the entire paragraph; we know the context. And I'm interested in particular in the lines I wanted to read out. "If Mrksic had ordered me to hand over the evacuees to the local Serbian TO, I would have obeyed the order on the condition that the evacuees were given no trouble. However, if I had been there alone as the most senior officer, I would have seen to it that the evacuees were taken to a safe place and would have sent the TO away. (I would have barred their presence)."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is that what is stated there, Mr. Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: First of all, was Dragi Vukosavljevic trying to warn you to do something similar to as described here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "to do something"?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To do as you stated in this statement, had you been at Ovcara and had you been the most senior-ranking officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But this is what is stated here. You said --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Did Dragi Vukosavljevic try to warn you that those evacuees should be taken someplace else and the TO members sent away?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Had you been the most senior officer, why wouldn't you have done that, as you stated here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had I been the most senior and had I been responsible, I would have secured them. I wasn't the most senior, however; it was Major Vukasinovic. He had brought them there and he was tasked with their security. This was -- what I tried to do with the prisoners can clearly be seen with the situation with the Mitnica group and the way I handled the situation there.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the last part of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: With the 80th Motorised Brigade and your members of the military police company as well as your officers -- on the 20th of November, together with your officers, with your military police company, and other members of the 80th Motorised Brigade, would you have been able to see this task through successfully had you had the orders and the authority you stated here?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no authority of command over the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But suppose you did. With the troops you commanded, could you have seen the tasks through successfully?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no powers over the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But assuming you had, my question was quite clear, and do not try to interrupt me. With the forces you had and considering the way you handled things the first time around, could you have done this successfully the second time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have had I been given the responsibility of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that you had the sufficient troops who could have seen that through?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the troops. Had I been given the task, I would have done so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Lukic, are you going to start? We have 15 minutes before the break. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think this was not recorded properly. I asked: "Would you have had sufficient forces to complete that task had you been entrusted with it?" And the answer was: "If I had been given the assignment, I would have had sufficient forces at my disposal to complete the task."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as was the case previously with the Mitnica group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've just checked the time. I may as well begin now, but then the next session would only be a one-hour session. It might be more helpful to have the break now, but it might be better to give the witness a chance to rest and then resume after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Lukic. We will have our break now. Since there has been a redaction, we will have half an hour break, so we will gather at 20 past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Again, good morning, Your Honours, good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vojnovic, good morning. I am Novak Lukic, one of Veselin Sljivancanin's Defence counsel. I will be asking you some questions. You have your own statements in front of you and some of the documents that we shall be looking at in search of answers. First I'll ask you a couple of questions. This was something that was raised by Mr. Moore at the beginning of his examination-in-chief, something about your statements. It is quite obvious that you have provided quite a number of those and you have given a lot of evidence on these events that you have been talking about here over the last couple of days. Some of those testimonies were quite extensive and quite detailed. You will agree with me on that, right? I mean, primarily in relation to Ovcara in Belgrade. You testified for two days. You were confronted with the testimonies of other witnesses, and you were asked a lot of questions. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In relation to your statement to the OTP, and you have that set of statements in front of you so you can have a look, please. Your statement to the OTP, there's one thing that I've noticed. This conversation went on for three days; 24th, 25th -- the 25th and 26th September, 2003, and the 2nd of October, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The best part of the conversation lasted for two days. The third day I only came back to go through the statement and sign it, but we finished most of the interview on the first two days.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you. Another thing that I've noticed is the OTP had a very strong team representing it. There was Mr. Theunens, there was Kristina Carey, and I realise that an observer was present from the General Staff of the armed forces, Dragan Dusenovic. He was there throughout, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a colonel representing the General Staff the first two days, not the third day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe that you provided detailed answers to a wide range of questions raised by the OTP in relation to just about everything they wanted to know about, and you probably had some answers. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, at least to the extent I now remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So much for the statements. Thank you. I'll ask you the usual question I ask witnesses here, something about my client. A couple of questions about Veselin Sljivancanin. You told Mr. Moore that when you arrived in Negoslavci you knew virtually none of the officers from the Guards Brigade. I do assume, however, that you met my client at the command of the operations group of the Guards Brigade. Did you know Sljivancanin back then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know a single officer from Operations Group South until my arrival in Negoslavci. It was in Negoslavci that I met the innermost circle of brigade commanders, including Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I concluded from your evidence - I'm now talking about the 20th of November alone, the afternoon hours - regardless of how long this took, throughout that time you did not see my client inside the hangar or around the hangar there. You didn't, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was your evidence in all the different trials in which you testified. Can you look at paragraph 46 of your statement to the OTP. You were shown a photograph of my client. I'll just read that to you, and you say: "Veselin Sljivancanin, I did not see him at Ovcara or at the meeting on the 20th of November, 1991, at the command post of the Guards Brigade. However, I was late to that meeting and by the time I arrived, the other officers were leaving already." This is what you stated back then. Just for the sake of precision, I will ask you to do this: Can you please get the transcript from the Belgrade trial, dated the 25th of November. You should have it right in front of you. The reference is page 20, and for the benefit of my learned friends and the Chamber, the English reference is page 23, line 8. You provided very specific answers to these questions, and I want that to be reflected in our records, too.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where exactly is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Page 20, the transcript is the 25th of November, 2004. Have you found that, the Belgrade Ovcara trial? Page 20. Further down the page, Deputy Prosecutor Dusan Knezevic, halfway down the page, this question: "I should like to know whether Major Sljivancanin was present when the witness Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic informed Colonel Mrksic of the situation with the prisoners."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Let us just finish this. I'll read the entire paragraph and then can you please start answering after that. "Presiding Judge: You did answer that question yesterday, didn't you? "Witness Vojnovic: What I said was I cannot confirm 100 per cent whether he was there or not. "Presiding Judge: But you did say no to that question yesterday. Right? "Witness Vojnovic: Well, I'm still saying the same thing. I did not see him. "Presiding Judge: Yesterday, when answering a question of mine to that effect, you answered no. You said that Mrksic, yourself, and Vukosavljevic were there, whereas you didn't see him. You are talking about a room where there are a number of people and that is now in this group. "Witness Vojnovic: I didn't see him then. I mean, Mrksic is quite a striking man. He stands out and people knew him. I think I would have noticed him, and I knew him. "Presiding Judge: Never mind noticed. Did you talk or didn't you? "Witness Vojnovic: I did not contact him personally, but I did not see him. I do not know whether he was there. "Presiding Judge: Sljivancanin, yes, probably, but he says Mrksic is tall and a striking man. He said 'Mrksic.' All right." The final question by the Prosecutor: "So was he in that room or wasn't he?" Your answer: "I did not see him." Mr. Vojnovic, there's a slight discrepancy there. Mrksic, his striking looks, then Sljivancanin, you were obviously talking about Sljivancanin. Do you still stand by everything you said in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see him then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Let's move on. Now, I'll ask you something else about my client, Mr. Sljivancanin. Let's go to the very end of the time-line, if I may put it that way, the meeting at Velepromet. My client says - and tell me if I am wrong - that the meeting was held on the day the Guards Brigade was about to leave, the 24th at about 1400 hours. That very day when the Guards Brigade was about to withdraw, there was this meeting at Velepromet, the one you described for us. Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure the meeting took place. What he said is true. I said that was just before the Guards Brigade left, but I didn't give the date. I thought it may have been a day or two earlier, but that makes no difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me jog your memory about something that my client claims. Mr. Vojnovic, do you remember that the main subject discussed at the meeting to which my client had been invited by the TO commanders was the fact that the TO commanders then requested from him that the money be handed over to them that the army had previously found in the Vukovar bank? Sljivancanin replied they couldn't have the money, that the money would be given to the civilian authorities once these had been established, that the money would then be returned. Do you remember that being the main subject discussed at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really remember that this was the crucial thing discussed at the meeting. They were saying things like that, but I'm not sure if that was the most important subject matter actually raised at the meeting. There were references later on to other requests for money, the money from the post office. And I know people were saying that they would be given the money through some other channels or through someone else's mediation. This may have been mentioned by Major Sljivancanin and it certainly was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it was also discussed later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Both Vujovic and Vujanovic were adamant about the money, weren't they? People from the TO staff, but Sljivancanin stood firm and refused to hand the money over to them, didn't he? Is this possible?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. It may have been like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on. You've talked a lot about the area of responsibility, about the relationships within OG South. You understand, given my client's profile, I'm especially interested in the relationships between the military police, the security, and the commander. So I'll ask you several questions about that. I believe the Prosecutor previously examined you on this. I heard - and I believe this is beyond dispute - that your military police company of the 80th Motorised Brigade remained there as a staff unit when you arrived in Negoslavci. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Right there, near the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: They were going about their regular duties in terms of providing security for the command post for the commander himself. There was a check-point, we heard; all of this was going on in Negoslavci. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In general terms, and I'm talking about the staff units that remained under your direct command, did any of those officers ever tell you about any lack of discipline in those units, disciplinary violations? I especially want to know about the military police company. Did any of the officers ever mention anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire unit was made up of reservists. It was difficult to mobilise. It was difficult to actually bring there. There were problems, there were a number of incidents, but nothing that would have caused any major concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose you received reports about this both from the chief of security and the company commander. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't much in touch with the company commander. He did come to see me once and he said a thing or two about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, we are on the verge of being cautioned by the interpreters. Please make a short pause so that the entire question and the entire answer may be recorded. I realise by looking at your CV that at one point in time you were a commander of a military police company. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You completed a six-month training course, specialised training, in Pancevo for military police officers. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, we've heard evidence before this Court and we've looked at the regulations. I don't want to press the issue -- well, depending on any answers I may be getting from you in due course, but what I want to know now is the provisions that were in force at the time when all of this was going on in Vukovar. You will agree with me that the rules governing the work of the armed forces are fundamental, the rules govern governing the military police in the armed forces, and the rules governing the work of the security officers in the armed forces. These are the main sources; right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on these regulations, who commands a military police company?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the regulations -- well, that could change. Sometimes it was a staff unit and sometimes it was directly under the command of the commander of a superior unit. But for the most part it would be the unit commander through his own technical organ, the chief of security.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that under the regulations the security organ is in command of the military police directly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they provide professional and technical guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. That's right. We have to look at the regulations. You have them right in front of you. I don't want to press this issue, but do you agree with me that a military police company is commanded by the company commander, and his superior officer, in terms of the chain of command, is the commander of a superior unit? A brigade, let us assume that for the time being, if it's a staff unit, and in terms of technical guidance, it is the security organ from the brigade command that is in charge of this unit. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the security organ makes proposals to his superior in terms of the chain of command, the brigade commander, the use of a military police company proposes measures in relation to the military police company but cannot directly issue an order except by the commander's approval. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I hope we don't have to go back to the rules and look at them just because of this, but still --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe you, too, have ... Just a minute, please. Let me ask the witness for his professional expertise. He seems to be extremely well-versed in these matters. Exhibit 107, the rules of service for the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, you have in front of you the rules of service both for the military police, but we'll not be looking at that now. I believe we've covered that ground, as it were. But can you please have a look at the rules of service for the security organ. This is Exhibit 107. Let's look at Article 16. Have you found it? I'm going to read it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The jurisdiction of the military police, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, it's the rules of service for the security organs. Article 16, controlling the security organs. We've marked it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's note: We don't have a copy of the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am reading. For the interpreters, I hope it will be slow enough. "Controlling the organs of security, Article 16. "The security organs -- the security organ is directly subordinated to the officer of the command of the unit or institution or the armed forces staff in whose establishment formation it is placed and is responsible for its work to that officer. Security organs of the JNA in organisations of the MVO are responsible to the federal secretary of the federal organ."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, we don't want to interpret the article, but it is clear that the security organ is directly subordinated to the command officer, or to say in the example of your particular unit, Dragi Vukosavljevic is immediately subordinated to you according to the line of command. And now we have Article 18, because we also discussed that. These are the relationships of the security organs between the commands at different levels. "The security organs --" I'm reading Article 18. "The security organs of the superior command unit, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces control in the expert sense the security organs in subordinated commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces; provide assistance to those organs; and organise, direct, coordinate, and inspect their work." You would agree with me that the relationship between the security organs at various levels is only at the expert level and there is no command or subordinate aspect there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So to conclude, in relation to Captain Vezmarovic, according to the line of command, only the brigade commander who could have commanded him -- or rather, you, Vukosavljevic would have guided his work from the expert aspect, and some other officer, for example, the Chief of Staff whom you mentioned, could have commanded Vezmarovic only if you authorised him to do that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Or any other officer if something was needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Right. But only in accordance with your approval?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume that your security chief, either at daily briefings or during the regular daily briefing, regularly informed you about all the information pertaining to his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He would inform the commander about any matters pertaining to his duties that he felt were necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you testified two days ago - this is on page 8826 of the transcript - when Mr. Moore asked you about the relationship -- you don't have that in front of you, I'm just going to read it to you. The relationship between Vukasinovic and Sljivancanin, you said, answer -- the Prosecutor asked you whether Sljivancanin had any duties in relation to your brigade. Your answer was: [In English] "I am not aware of that now, except that he was the chief of Operative Group South and he probably cooperated with my security organs." [Interpretation] You probably meant chief of security and not chief, but I'm interested in something else. You said that he probably cooperated with your security organ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's how it is in practice. The security organs of the superior and subordinate command mostly cooperate.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you said, and I am concluding, because Vukosavljevic informed you personally -- I spoke with Sljivancanin, we exchanged information, or something else. When you said "probably" --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
