utterances.text: He never said anything like that, but as far as I know, I did -- I think that he did cooperate with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware that your security organ, from the moment when he -- or, rather, you came to Negoslavci, had continuous contact with the Kragujevac security organ on the -- of the 24th, did you have information about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no information of -- about him maintaining contact with anyone from the Kragujevac Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My question is not clear. I am -- I meant the Kragujevac Corps, the 24th Corps - and this is page 52, line 2 - and we have an answer to that question. Did Vukosavljevic inform you that along the expert line he had contacts, information, reporting with the security organs from the 1st Military District who were in Sid at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the details, but I know that he did have some contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were these contacts maintained from early November while you were still part of OG South? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, and Dragi could not have been in touch immediately. He needed to see exactly where he was, assess the situation, but he probably established contact quite quickly. He probably found those people from the superior command quite quickly and that he got in touch with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're now moving to another topic. You testified that you were regularly at OG South meetings in the Negoslavci command, which were usually held in the afternoon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that at any of those meetings there was talk about the evacuation of the hospital and there was also talk about who would be carrying out the evacuation of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was no discussion about that and I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. Let us continue. We're moving to another topic now. From your testimony during these two days, I have drawn the conclusion and I gained the impression that you knew Major Ljubisa Vukasinovic from before, before the time that you said you saw him at the hangar. My question is: Where did you know him from?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew him from the OG South command post. I didn't know him before I came. That's where I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The command post of the operations group?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's where I saw him in the group of the officers and senior officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know specifically what his post was? You said Sljivancanin's deputy, but I would like a soldier's precision. Do you know exactly what his post was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his specific establishment post, but if Sljivancanin was the chief of security of Operations Group South, then according to my logic and according to the establishment formation, he should have been a clerk in the security organ. As to whether this was really so or not is something that I really cannot assert.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to tell you, and I'm sure my learned friend from the Prosecution would like to know what my position is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the post.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. I'm going to repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Major Ljubisa Vukasinovic was the assistant chief of security in the Guards Motorised Brigade for staff and police affairs at that time. Are you aware that at the time Major Ljubisa Vukasinovic was also the local commander of Negoslavci, at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that, but I did read that just now in these reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to digress now. I see, Mr. Vojnovic, that very often when you testify you testify about something that you learned later. What I would like you to do is, when you say something like that, if you could please tell us when you heard it. But it's all right. Yes, let's go on, let's go on. It's not a problem. I see that you followed the testimony of other people and that you have information that you acquired later, and this is something that always needs to be told.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did follow the testimony. I also have some notes. I don't have them with me, but I do have them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time did you hear that in Negoslavci, in Vukovar, and at Ovcara on that 20th of November, there were also certain officers from the security administration and from the security organ of the 1st Military District? I'm specifically talking about the 19th and 20th of November. Did you hear that at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't really be certain about that -- I mean, I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see that you followed the trial, but don't tell me that you heard that during the trial. But later, subsequently during those days, did you hear those names and were these names familiar to you, such as Kijanovic, Tomic, Bogdan Vujic, Muncan --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vujic Bogdan is a name familiar to me. Muncan too. The others I don't know. Vujic also I'm aware of. It's a name that is familiar to me. Vujic is known to me from some testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell me -- I mentioned, besides line, up there, 53, besides Kijanovic, I also mentioned Vujic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Line 55, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Slavko Tomic. I also mentioned the surname Muncan and you said you knew that. Did you hear that name then?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of the Muncan last name, I don't know in what context. As far as Bogdan Vujic is concerned, I read about him from some testimony. I don't know which one. I don't know before which court, at which organ. In any case, I heard that he had testified somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At that time during the meetings at the Negoslavci command, did you see then-Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him once in the OG South command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time, did you have information that he was included in the negotiations on the surrender of the Mitnica group and also in the evacuation of the civilians from Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that later and I saw him, that he was at Ovcara before the Mitnica group left, before they were taken to Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So on that day - we won't say which day - but on the day that the Mitnica group was leaving, on that day, the hangar in the morning, that's when you saw Nebojsa Pavkovic there at Ovcara. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one more question on this topic. How far was your Negoslavci command post from the command post of the Guards Brigade or, rather, the OG South command post?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was 1 to 2 kilometres at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We're moving to the next topic. I'm going to ask you a couple of questions now about the Mitnica group evacuation. We presented considerable number of written exhibits and there were quite a number of testimony that the Mitnica group was accommodated in the afternoon on the 18th to the Ovcara hangar and that they left the hangar on the 19th in the morning. But -- well, you've already said that you are not so good with the dates, so we are going to move on. You said that you could have received that assignment either from Mrksic or from Panic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one moment. Can you please take the operations diary --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is Exhibit 371.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just very briefly like to look at the first page of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all right if the witness doesn't have a copy. Perhaps we can just look at it on the screen. Could we just look at the first page of the diary. Can we please zoom in on this? The lower portion of the page, please. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is your brigade's operations log. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One thing I want to know about - we haven't heard a great deal about that - column number 4. It reads: Signature, received - as far as I can see - recipient's signature and sender's signature. I think that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So what sort of information is entered here into this column number 4 of the operations log?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's self-explanatory, isn't it? Whoever enters a particular piece of information into the operations log is someone who forwards the information, and whoever was on duty was supposed to enter it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I personally - tell me if I am wrong --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think the information entered here is the information provided by the person who informs the duty officer about whatever information is supposed to be entered. We have your name in several different places. I suppose the information came from you; it wasn't that you entered the information or recorded it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. There's somebody providing information and there's somebody recording information.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So here we see the name of whoever provides information to whoever keeps the log. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's fine. So much for the log. We've all seen enough of it and we'll be glad to see the back of it, in a manner of speaking, and I suppose the same applies to you. I do want to know something else, though. You were asked by both Mr. Moore and Mr. Vasic about Captain Karanfilov. I'm talking about the 18th, I'm talking about the Mitnica group, I'm talking about their day, as it were, when they arrived. You said you didn't know him at the time, you didn't know if he was there or not. And then Mr. Vasic asked you yesterday, he confronted you with your own statement from the Novi Sad investigation. This might have been the person you saw back then -- well, I'll move on to something else because there's something else I want to ask you about. I want to know about some facts you stated at the Belgrade trial. Would you have issued an order to Vezmarovic to take orders from Karanfilov? That is what I really want to know, and you provided a very specific answer at the Belgrade trial to this one. Therefore, could you please go back to your statement -- or your evidence, dated the 25th of November, 2004.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of my learned friends and the Chamber, the reference is the 25th of November. The English reference is page 2, line 32, third paragraph from the bottom up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And for you, Witness, the B/C/S reference -- or rather, the reference in our language -- just a minute, please. Page 2, sir. I was instructed by the Chamber the last time around not to read the question. It says: "Presiding Judge," ten lines from the bottom up, just by way of an example, but the Presiding Judge is here confronting you with the statement of another witness and we have different rules governing our procedure here. It's not the same as the rules that apply back where we come from. I'll just read your answer: "I did not know Captain Karanfilov either; that is for sure. I only knew Vukasinovic and I may have seen him at some meetings." "Presiding Judge --" I'm skipping the first sentence -- "Is it true or not that you told Vezmarovic that he was to take orders from Karanfilov or not?" Answer -- your answer: "I did not say that to Vezmarovic. "Presiding Judge: He says that you did and that is why I am asking you, that is why I am telling you this." Your answer: "As far as I can now remember, I did not say that to Vezmarovic. I heard that Vezmarovic said that he only took orders from Karanfilov. "Presiding Judge: What did you hear?" Your answer: "I heard that Vezmarovic said that he only took orders from Karanfilov, as he was a security officer and that was a military police unit. "Presiding Judge: When did you hear this from Vezmarovic?" Your answer: "I later heard this from someone out there that Vezmarovic had stated that he would only be taking orders from the security officer, from Karanfilov." Let us now move on to page 7. That is the B/C/S reference. The English reference is page 7, line 23. Your answer seems to be very determined here. "Presiding Judge: In the investigation procedure -- you also said possibly it was I who told Captain Vezmarovic that he was to take orders from Karanfilov." Your answer: "I did not personally tell him that he was to take orders. I later heard -- I did not hear that I told him this to do that, but I only heard that he said that he would only take orders from Vezmarovic -- or rather, from Karanfilov, him being a security officer and that he would obey his orders." Is that accurate? Did I read this accurately, the exchange between you and the Presiding Judge?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with your own evidence from the Belgrade Ovcara trial? You did not order Vezmarovic to take orders from Captain Karanfilov; rather, you said you heard this later on, that you had heard him saying this. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard him saying this, that he would be taking orders from organ Karanfilov. I think he was a major at the time or something, from Karanfilov. I don't remember actually raising this issue with him. I see that Karanfilov is involved, so probably after all that happened. There may have been some omissions or something, but certainly no additions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us try to be as precise as possible. You don't remember giving Vezmarovic an order like that, do you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And let me add this for your information and also to corroborate my own theory: Karanfilov was a security clerk in a battalion-level unit. You will agree with me, won't you, that in view of his position he had no authority to impart any orders to anyone at all. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I hear of him being a security officer in a battalion-level unit. I, myself, believed that he was some sort of a clerk or something from the security of OG South. I really didn't know his assignment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: Could I just ask my learned friend -- I know there's translation of the word "clerk," and I've seen that on several occasions. Our understanding that that word doesn't mean "clerk," that in actual fact it means "staff officer." In English it tends to mean -- there's a rather big difference, and that's the third time it's happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is up to Mr. Moore to have this clarified in re-examination. When I say "clerk" that perfectly corresponds with my information. Yes, of course, a staff officer is one thing and a clerk is a different thing. But I think the word "referent" is exactly the word used by the interpretation service. "Staff officer," that is a very broad concept and can entail a lot of different things, but certainly this particular witness does not have any information about that, and I believe we will be able to establish all these facts later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, however, based on all the regulations that we looked at a while ago -- you've seen those. You've given me all the answers in keeping with those regulations. A security officer cannot impart any orders to anyone from the military police. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following approval from one of the superior officers, yes, they could. My approval specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Following your approval, a security officer could, couldn't he? Another simple question: A security officer from a superior command conveying an order to the military police of a subordinate unit, what would the military police company commander first be expected to do upon receiving an order like that? What would be the first thing they should do?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He should first inform the security officer. But it is very seldom that assignments are given to the company without the security officer's knowledge or the commander's knowledge or the Chief of Staff's knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I won't ask you any questions about the day when the large number of buses arrived, but I will ask you about something else. However, this is outside the scope of anything that you have been asked so far, so please focus on this. I think you told Mr. Borovic today that you had had some of your units attached to other units in the Sotin area. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your duty and the duty of the command of OG South was to inform the superior command about the killing or wounding of any of the members of your units. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If a soldier or an officer from your unit were killed I suppose you would have to inform your superior command; the OG South command in your case.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 421.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will see a document come up on your screen shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please just zoom in on the upper half of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, this is a regular combat report of the OG South command dated the 20th of November, 1991, 1800 hours. This was sent to the command of the 1st Military District and to the SSNO cabinet. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2 of the same document, please. The lower half of the page, if you can please zoom in, where it says "paragraph 3."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sir, what we see here is information on those killed, seriously or slightly wounded on the previous day from the previous report. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. As for those killed, are there any members of the 80th Brigade? I'm talking about the night between the 19th and the 20th, in OG South. Please wait for my question. Please say it now. Do you see anyone there or not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see -- just a minute, please. Thank you. No further questions about this document. At any rate, my question is -- well, let's try to tackle it this way: Do you remember if within your brigade if any members of your brigade were killed on those days?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, none. I know what the total was of those killed throughout our time there, throughout our time in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But none of your soldiers were killed on those days throughout the area covered by your brigade. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, none at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to the 20th of November now. I will try - this is will no doubt be easy - to sum up what you say you saw in the hangar. I can't help but observe that there are some discrepancies in your evidence, even over the last two days. You arrive at the hangar sometime in the afternoon. You stand outside the hangar for a while. Once everyone is inside, you join them inside. The highest-ranking person you see there is Major Ljubisa Vukasinovic. You ask him who these people are. He says: These are people from the hospital. You then call for help. You say you called for help even before you entered the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it was before or after, but I did call for help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Two of your officers arrived, Vukic and Dacic, with a group of soldiers. You tell them to go and speak to Vukasinovic, and the next thing you do is you leave. You claim the whole thing took about 30 minutes, although you told my learned friend Mr. Borovic today that it may have taken longer. Be that as it may, this was an attempt to sum up what you, yourself, stated. Has that been your evidence over the last two days, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were not outside the hangar at the moment the buses arrived, but, rather, as the buses were already being emptied, and then the gauntlet and everything else you went on to describe. So this is the point in time when you arrive outside the hangar. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As soon as you entered the hangar, and inside you saw Vukasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This was after the last people from the bus were brought inside.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you saw someone making some kind of list in the hangar during the time you were there, and you saw that the rope was set up. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you said that the rope was set up, you didn't explain what that was. Was it to separate the prisoners from the other people? Was that the purpose of the rope?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the purpose of the rope. It was used to separate the prisoners from the members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we move into private session for a moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You testified that you don't remember -- or rather, that you did not see Lieutenant-Colonel Panic at that time when you were in front of the hangar but that later you heard from him - you probably followed his testimony, as you say - that he confirmed at that time that he was in front of the hangar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it from him directly, that he was there, I didn't see him, and I also heard it from the man that was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I'm going to ask you something else now. Do you remember - and I think I read that in some of your testimonies, there were many of them so I cannot really recall which one - but do you remember that at the time you saw an unknown colonel as he was leaving the hangar in a Renault 4 vehicle and leaving Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see a Renault 4, but it did not go out of the hangar. I saw a Renault 4 standing there. I saw a military person in uniform, the licence plates were Sremska Mitrovica plates, and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that was a colonel by rank; is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was a colonel, but I am not sure. He left right away. He got into the car and he left.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think it is time for our break now, and then we'll be moving to a different topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Public session -- sorry, we are in public. I was confused. Okay, so we will adjourn for -- oh, I'm sorry, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour, I am Phil Weiner for the Office of the Prosecutor. We were advised by the Defence that they will be spending at least another session with this witness, and then if you add to that examination in chief -- sorry, redirect examination, that should take most of the day. We have the next witness here. Since we will probably be running most of the day with this witness, may I release that witness until tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Weiner. Mr. Lukic, can you confirm that timing?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can confirm that we will need more than one session, at least for my cross-examination. We might even take to the rest of the day. I have a lot of questions arising from the questions of my colleagues, so in any case I think that it will not be possible to begin with a new witness today, especially since Mr. Moore also needs time for the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Okay, Mr. Weiner, you may release the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Okay. We will adjourn now and convene at 1.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.33 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Before I continue, I just wanted to correct a thing for the transcript. Page 66, line 10, there was my question which hasn't been recorded adequately. The reference should have mentioned page 66, line 3, and instead what has been recorded was 663.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you about the colonel whom you saw leave in a Renault 4. Timewise, did you see him leave before you entered the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to clarify something. I didn't tell that to Mr. Moore either, and I apologise -- or to anyone else, for that matter. I told this only to the chief of security when I gave my first testimony or first statement, and that was that while the prisoners were entering the hangar I looked up and in a distance, some 20 to 30 metres away, I saw a colonel in a uniform standing next to a Renault 4. And he was observing the struggle I had to get the prisoners inside the hangar. I approached him immediately, I addressed him. I said: Colonel, sir, what is this all about? Please help me to get those people inside the hangar. He didn't say anything. He got in the car, in that Renault 4, and left. He was somewhat short. I don't know his name and I don't remember having seen him ever afterwards. That's what I stated the chief of security when I gave my first statement, but he hasn't entered that into it although I signed it. I also mentioned that that person resembled him and then he jumped up to his feet and said: "No, no, I wasn't there."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the plates were those from Sremska Mitrovica. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you said that the person resembled a person to whom you gave the statement, you mean Mr. Gajic at the security directorate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was joking somewhat. He was of the same height but he didn't look like Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you also mentioned that in your testimony at the Belgrade Ovcara case?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The way I phrased it here and now, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. This is the first time I've heard some of the details and I believe this is new for all those in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first time they can hear it. I didn't know the man, and Colonel Galic [as interpreted] did not include that in the statement and I basically kept silent from then on, although I shouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And because he failed to enter that in the statement, you thought it necessary to avoid mentioning the fact ever after, and you did provide additional statements subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less that is as you described.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You used to go to the command of OG South and the Guards Brigade to meetings and you don't remember having seen him there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only way I remember him is the way I described him; a thin, short man.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard testimonies here that there was some other lieutenant-colonels and colonels at that time during the afternoon and that some senior officers came from the security directorate as well. Do you remember seeing anyone else of that approximate rank?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see anyone with any rank. I kept repeating, and I probably overdid it, that I saw Vukasinovic and another group of people without any hats but in proper uniform, although I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more question before we go into the hangar, so to say. When you were leaving the hangar and leaving Ovcara, the buses that had been there, did they leave when you left for Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They left one after another. They were parked on the road closer to the western part of the hangar, but I didn't see them when I was leaving the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm interested in the part when you left Ovcara.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As regards your leaving Ovcara, when you came out of the hangar did you see any pit with any corpses next to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you see a tractor in front of the hangar?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or a backhoe loader?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now move into the hangar itself. There is Vukasinovic, there is the rope, there is the person compiling the list. You've described those in detail. Then Vukic and Dacic came and they report to Vukasinovic, and then you leave.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to see Vukic; he was the group commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to read out a portion of your testimony of two days ago in the same context. That is page 8845, the transcript of the 15th of May. [In English] "They arrived headed by reserve Captain Vukic. He arrived with 15 or 20 men. There were no military police. Perhaps some of them did have military police belts on, but they were not actually the military police because Vezmarovic at that time was still in Sremska Mitrovica." [Interpretation] According to your testimony on the first day here, the 15th, when you testified in chief, when you came to the hangar, there was no Vezmarovic to be seen, neither -- nor was Mr. Dragi Vukosavljevic there, your chief of security. The only person you could see there was Ljubisa Vukasinovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the first moment I saw Vukasinovic only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when you gave your statement to the OTP investigators, the investigators gave you your statement before the military court. You had no corrections to make, apart from the fact that you failed to mention Mrksic. That is what can also be seen in your statement given to the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you testified in the proceedings in Novi Sad before Judge Alimpic, you were also faced with your statement given to the military court and you said that you stood by it in full. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic referred you to that statement on several occasions, but I need to go back to it yet again. Please could you take your statement given before the military court. Page 3 in the English, line 9, this is what you said before the military court. I'm reading from the bottom part. "In the hangar there were those for whom I thought were paramilitaries, perhaps around 20 of them." And today -- yesterday you explained that there were more. "They were guarding those in the hangar and they were all armed. I did not particularly notice that anyone in the hangar was maltreated except when somebody recognised someone, they would approach them and utter a threat or use abusive language, but nothing more than that, at least while I was there." I'm interested in the following portion in particular: "I warned the men in the hangar to treat correctly the people they referred to as their prisoners of war and not mistreat them, stressing that they should take care of how they treat them and behave towards them. After the warning I gave in the hangar, I did not notice that there was any mistreatment anymore." That's what you stated then. Does this jog your memory that back in 1998 you probably remember those events better than you do today, and that is that you actually spoke to those TO members?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who I spoke with, but each new testimony jogged my memory, I would remember additional things, and I thought it necessary to mention here that after what I saw in front of the hangar and after what I realised they were doing, I warned them not to mistreat them any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: A few lines further down: "At that time in the hangar or outside of the hangar I saw no other regular units of the JNA or any of its members. I only saw those men who I judged were some kind of paramilitary army, given the clothes they had on. None of them had either JNA uniforms or cap," and so on and so forth. In the subsequent statements, you confirmed that there were some additional JNA people there; and then back in 1999 you stated that you saw no one from the JNA in the hangar. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, apart from Vukasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But in this statement you don't mention Vukasinovic, Dacic, Vukic, or anyone else. You remembered that later.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never failed to mention Vukasinovic. He was the only one that I could recognise. I have always claimed that he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So as not to waste anymore time, perhaps during the break you could go again through your statement to the military court, and there is not a single mention of Vukasinovic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps Mr. Moore could corroborate that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: We don't corroborate that. We have, actually, a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this will be clarified in redirect. I don't think I saw any mention of Vukasinovic in this statement, but then again, I may be wrong. Perhaps Mr. Moore will deal with this in his redirect.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this statement given to the military court, did you ever mention that you asked for some assistance?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. The only way for me to know is to go back and read the whole thing. That was given in 1998. I don't remember having said that, but I did ask for assistance and it is certain that Vukasinovic was in the hangar. I'm absolutely certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. One step at a time. Mr. Vojnovic, I need to describe our position here. Based on the information we have, together with the OTP, as regards Mr. Vukasinovic, he did indeed state that when the last of the buses arrived he was there. He said so himself, so I'm not trying to deny the fact whether Vukasinovic was there at the time when the buses were there, but I'm just trying to point out that you failed to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I -- perhaps I may have omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There are some other facts that they be disputed, and I wanted to discuss that as far as Major Vukasinovic. You described the people you saw with Major Vukasinovic and you said they were wearing M-77 uniforms but you couldn't tell whether they were soldiers or officers, but those were standard-issue uniforms for both file and rank.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember Vukasinovic, was he wearing the same uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he had the same uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that he didn't have a cap.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that he wore this M-77 uniform.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I believe it was M-77 or whether it was a combination of two types of uniforms, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Vojnovic, some facts are particularly important. If you don't know, please state so. What's important to me is that you did see Ljubisa Vukasinovic. As you say, you exchanged a couple of words with him. My question is: Was he wearing the same kind of uniform as the persons surrounding him? Can you see the image in your mind's eye?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't be 100 per cent certain. I can't commit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yet you remember exactly what the people around him were wearing. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you don't know what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember. You're pressing me on this, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. Let's move on. Yesterday you told Mr. Vasic that you had requested officers from your command in Negoslavci, two officers, as you specified, and some soldiers, because you know -- you knew that Vezmarovic was away at the time. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You told Mr. Borovic today that you thought that later on Dragi Vukosavljevic returned with Vukic and Dacic. They came. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do remember that -- or is that what you told Mr. Borovic? Do you remember him coming with those two men?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember for sure, but I think he came with them. It's because the vehicle, I don't know who he possibly could have come with.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's look at these facts, what you find in the hangar. In the Belgrade Ovcara trial, page 67 of the first day of your testimony, the 24th of November. Page 67. The English reference is 97, page 97. The following words in English: [In English] "... what I could." [Interpretation] I will now read out to you a slightly longer portion. Have you found 67?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The 24th.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite there yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] "I did what I could." [Interpretation] In English, it says, "I did what I could." I'm not sure where on the page that should be.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And our reference is --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our reference is 67, page 67, the 24th of November. You got that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a large portion, but I'll be asking you questions as I go along, because I think there are a couple of discrepancies in relation to your testimony of two days ago. "I did what I could. Later on what I saw around the hangar was some people coming and going. I don't know now how. I can't say for sure how Dragi Vukosavljevic happened to be there, this captain of mine. He was the chief of security, and while this commotion was going on, he proposed -- or rather, he asked whether we should do anything else and asked what it was that we could do to help those people to keep them from being mistreated. We agreed that a military police detachment should come, one of ours from Negoslavci; a Pinzgauer with seven, eight, or nine soldiers, I don't know how many exactly. However, in the meantime, Captain Vezmarovic had arrived." Here is where I'll pause. You agree with me that your testimony in Belgrade is not consistent with what you told us here two days ago. In the Belgrade trial, it comes across that you are conferring with him: Should we call a military police unit or not? And at this point in time Vezmarovic arrives. That's what you said in Belgrade. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there with Dragi. We talked about this. We did ask for help to be sent. I don't know if Vezmarovic came first. I still think Vukic was the first to come, but I can't be certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One thing at a time, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. "Vezmarovic, I can't remember his name, but no matter. It's clear who we're talking about. All right. When he came back from Sremska Mitrovica, he was driving a group of prisoners, members of the Croatian army, led by Filip Karaula. He returned to the command to report that he had completed the task as necessary and that those people had been handed over smoothly. Someone told him -- someone at the brigade command told him that there was some sort of a mess happening at Ovcara, and he immediately went there to see at his own initiative and out of curiosity and also for reasons of self-promotion. He went there to see for himself. This coincided with the very same thing that we were thinking, that there should be a reinforcement, a military police unit, so there he was." Further down: "In the hangar I saw that Vezmarovic put up a rope separating those people from the group that had brought them there, so to speak, with a rope. I saw that a desk was placed there. Someone was making list. I saw that. Whether it was finished or not, be that as it may, this is what I saw." I'll continue reading, but let me first ask you about this. At the Belgrade trial a year and a half ago, you describe Vezmarovic's arrival, him putting up that rope, and you say you saw the whole thing happen. In Belgrade a year and a half ago you remembered all these things. I see that there is another discrepancy. Can you tell us now: Were you, in fact, speaking the truth in Belgrade when you said this, that you saw Vezmarovic arrive and put up a rope?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see Vezmarovic at Ovcara. I don't know if I saw him the moment he arrived. I don't know who arrived first, again, whether it was Vukic or he. Anyway, they were both there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine, but you will agree that there is at least a slight discrepancy from your present testimony.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Let's move on. You testified under oath in Belgrade and the same seems to be the case now, but that was the way you remembered things at the time. It's as simple as that. Let me move on. "In the hangar I saw for the first time since I entered Major Vukasinovic. Major Vukasinovic, he is from the Guards Brigade, Major Sljivancanin's deputy then he was. He was standing at a distance from that rope, or rope, whatever I should call it, about 10 metres away, and he was watching what was going on. I approached him and asked him what this was, where all these people were from, who was this and what was going on, and he told me something, but now I really can't remember the details of what it was that he said. I surveyed the situation a little more and realised that things were back to normal. Some of those people in there - what should I call them? - detainees, people, civilians, were standing along the hangar wall. Some were actually sitting on the ground. There was some hay, and some were sitting on the floor. I mean there was some kind of order when Vezmarovic arrived, excuse me, in the hangar. I thought, therefore, that there was nothing there for me to do, although I could not understand at all how this could have happened and that I, as the subordinate commander, had known nothing about it." We all know that there's an audio recording of the Belgrade trial. You spoke these words and you understand that you did, indeed, say this at the trial in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, the first discrepancy I can notice is you say you address Major Vukasinovic. You don't know what he told you a year and a half ago, and two days ago you tell us he spoke to you and he told you these were people from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is it that jogged your memory in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, events. I read reports from the trial. I read Major Vukasinovic, who told me there and who stated that he knew that the members of the prisoners would be surrendering or would be handed over, that they were surrendering, not that they were being beaten but that the TO people were interrogating them, or what should I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So this jogged your memory that he told you these were people from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and this was confirmed by Lieutenant-Colonel Panic that he knew that people from the hospital would surrender to the TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I do believe I have to interrupt you, Mr. Vojnovic. Don't draw your own conclusions based on what you heard, what another person told you. Rather, please, if your memory is jogged by what somebody else said about something that you remember because now you are giving us other people's accounts and some of your own conclusions. If you remember something based on something that you heard later, you may as well tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard later --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- from Lieutenant-Colonel Panic that a decision was made.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We know that. We know that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't know that. Everybody seems to have known. Only we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's fine, but Mr. Moore has something to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: All I wish to submit is a witness is entitled to give an account of what he has been told by another person who may well be a participant in what I would call the act. It may go to weight in relation to the evidence itself, but it does not mean it's inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: Thank you for that, Mr. Moore. I think you're right it's not inadmissible, but I think it's important for Mr. Lukic to identify those parts which are direct memory and those parts which are indirect memory. So, please employee, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I just -- I mean, I think the witness provided a far broader explanation than I wanted, a far broader one, and that's what I asked him, what jogged his memory, what caused him to remember that he was told this by Ljubisa Vukasinovic, but he didn't remember that a year and a half ago --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As well as his testimony and his statement, and I still have all that written down in my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you say it was from his statement, which I believe you read in the newspapers, you understood that he told you that those were people from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he told me so on the spot that those people were from the hospital, and this is something I read later on. His testimony, I mean, what he testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Vojnovic, please. Did you -- I mean, when reading the various testimonies of Ljubisa Vukasinovic, hear that he testified about telling you that those were people from the hospital? Did you ever read anywhere that he so testified when you now remembered?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, but I'm telling you he informed me that those were people from the hospital. Informed in the hangar. I may have omitted that, but in all my further testimony, I kept pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. In Belgrade on the 24th of November, 2004, you testified for two days, for a full two days. Not a single word about Vukic arriving at Ovcara. Not a single word. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I just didn't remember at the time. If you hadn't reminded me about the colonel today --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you remembered when you heard what Vukic's testimony had been about. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you actually meet Vukic and Dacic? You say you met Vezmarovic and Dragi Vukosavljevic. Can you just wait a minute, please. Did you actually meet at any time before or after your testimony Svetolik [phoen] Vukic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not meet Svetolik Vukic in any way -- any way after his testimony sometime.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But that was before you came here to testify. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no -- well, yeah, yeah, before this testimony, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You talked and he jogged your memory about all these various points, about the exchange between him and Vukasinovic, that sort of thing, and so on and so forth. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you never remembered that earlier on, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. In answer to a question by Mr. Vasic yesterday - the page reference is 8959 - you said: [In English] "When help had arrived from the brigade command led by Vukic, when I went inside the hangar, when I realised Vukasinovic was there, he told me who these people were and then there were a group of soldiers that was brought over, between 15 or 20 of them. I thought to myself, here was a man from my support command. I supposed that he had been given assignment. I offered him my help, and he refused." [Interpretation] This was on page 8959 of yesterday. Do you recall saying that like that yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Another correction: The page was 8959. And then you said yesterday to my colleague Vasic that you offered assistance and that he refused.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, just three pages before that, I found -- just three pages before that, page 8596, Vasic asked you -- [In English] "... Vukasinovic if he needed any assistance." The page is 8956. Your answer was: [No interpretation]. [Interpretation] So you gave two different answers on the same facts.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I offered assistance and he refused. I didn't offer it directly but I did it through Vukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your answer to Mr. Vasic was quite a definite one and this was page 8956, decisive answer. [In English] "Did you ask Major Vukasinovic if he needed any assistance?" [Interpretation] Your answer: [In English] "No, I didn't."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask the major directly. I sent Captain Vukic to him to speak to him and ask him if he needed help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You explained that nicely to us. Let's move on. Do you recall that during the time you were in the hangar, whether some people were taken to the side -- taken aside, people who claimed to be JNA soldiers, they didn't even enter the hangar because they were separated outside of the hangar. Do you remember anything like that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that. People were going in and out of the hangar, returning. They were talking to somebody. I don't remember anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. I have to go back to the transcript of the day before again. Please don't mind that I am going so much into details. This is important for both you and me so that we could establish the facts. Testimony from two days ago, page 8845. It's not clear to me what you answered in reply to Mr. Moore's question, which was as follows: [In English] "Why did you leave the hangar?" [Interpretation] Your answer: [In English] "First of all, I left the hangar because I wanted to ask for assistance and security from my brigade command. They headed -- They arrived headed by Reserve Captain Vukic." [Interpretation] I'm asking you -- now, Moore asked you why you left and you said you went to summon assistance, but I see in your testimony that you didn't go until they came. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you now please tell the Trial Chamber -- please, could you repeat your answer, it was not recorded, but could you please wait a little bit. Can you please repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know where it was that I looked for Vukic. All I know is what I told him once he arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Who was Captain or Captain First Class Vukic in your command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vukic was the chief of the PNHBO in my command. He was a reserve officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. And who was Captain Dacic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dacic, yes, Dacic. Yes, I can't remember his Christian name. He was, I think, an artillery desk officer in the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was also a reserve captain. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a reserve captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you remember his face? Do you remember seeing him, that he arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dacic, yes, I know what he looks like, but I don't recall seeing him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said today that it's possible that your security chief Vukosavljevic also came with them. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do know that Dacic and Vukic were close, that they spent a lot of time in each other's company, not just there but before that, too, and that's probably why they came together.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that Captain Vukic's arrival was something that you never mentioned in any of the statements that are in front of you. You didn't mention it to the OTP or before the military court or to the Novi Sad investigative judge or in your testimony in the Belgrade Ovcara case. Vujovic you mentioned for the first time now following Vukic's testimony which you heard. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since yesterday and the day before, I am not counting, but you really mentioned the name of this Vukic 15 times or more. I obviously think that, for you, you consider that to be an important fact, to mention him here.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The man came in compliance with a summons, an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So how do you explain the fact that you never remembered this man before now?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't remember him. Just like perhaps there's some other details that a person might not recall. I really didn't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you knew all the details of his testimony in the Belgrade Ovcara trial besides this dialogue with Vukasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not really. It was just a small article and he explained about what I was talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It would mean a lot to me if you were to tell me in which newspaper you read that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I will take it upon myself to send that article clipping to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would be very grateful. And you further assert that you sent Vukic to Vukasinovic and that you then left and that they later, as you testified on the first day, told you after a couple of days at the command that Vukasinovic told Vukic that he was free to go and that he then practically left.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that he had no assignment for him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Went back to the command. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm asking you this: You ordered that assistance be sent to you. This assistance arrived. And you ordered Vukic to report to Vukasinovic. Please tell me: Did you order Vukic to return once Vukasinovic allegedly told him that there was nothing for him to do, or did Vukic come on his own initiative?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When actually Vukasinovic ordered him that he was free to return to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ordered him?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This man asked him if he had an assignment for him. He said, no, he didn't have an assignment. Again he asked him: Can I return to the unit? And this man said, yes, you can, so he returned to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. What was your order then? That assistance needed to come to help with the security? That was your order. Vukic came in compliance with your order.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The order was carried out, order was established, the prisoners entered the hangar, so there was no longer any need for him to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But did you issue him an order to go back? You ordered him to come, so who can order him to go back? Who can tell him to go back other than the person who issued the order?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at this point Vukasinovic was the most senior-ranking person there, so Vukasinovic could do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You claim that Vukasinovic was the most senior-ranking person there. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He had the rank of major and came from the superior command, according to you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the hangar, does he have a higher rank and position than you do?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not stay in the hangar the whole time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the point when you saw him and when Vukic came, did Vukasinovic Ljubisa, have a higher rank than you, and we know that he did not, and did he occupy a higher position?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not, but he was the only person in charge and was tasked with bringing the prisoners to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I'm asking you the following: Were you present when the buses were arriving in a column to Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not present when they came in a column to Ovcara; they were already parked there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. You did not see who was at the head of the column and who brought the buses to Ovcara. You didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We heard from your testimony that you heard that Lieutenant-Colonel Panic was there, and today we heard that there was also some colonel there who left.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You cannot rule out that they were at the head of the column when the buses arrived. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I really cannot rule that out. I cannot say who was at the head of the column.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Ljubisa Vukasinovic did not tell you that he was the person in charge of the evacuation then. You didn't talk with him about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I read that in later reports, that he was conducting this evacuation operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you don't know who brought the column and who was the person in charge of the people who brought the prisoners to the hangar. You don't know that, you didn't know it then when you were talking with Ljubisa Vukasinovic, but this was something that you heard later while reading the statements or testimonies. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by reading, and of course it seemed natural to me that he was the only most senior-ranking person from the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm now going back to the previous question. Was Ljubisa Vukasinovic more senior by the nature of his post or was he lower in his duties than you were in both of your posts? It's a simple question.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a man from the superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I entirely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I don't know how many times I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this -- very well. Who is your superior officer in Vukovar in 1991 when you joined the Operations Group South? What was your superior officer?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The commander of the operations group.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: South.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We all know what the principle of the singleness and unity of command is. You know that principle.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And subordination.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was Ljubisa Vukasinovic of a higher rank in relation to you by his rank and position? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: I object to that question. The witness has asked -- been asked this question probably ten times and he's answered it equally ten times. He has a perception of it. And in my submission Mr. Lukic has had the answer many, many times. It's a question of the superior command, and the question has been asked so many times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT
utterances.text: I think it has been asked a lot of times, yesterday also by Mr. Vasic. So I think we have gone as far as we can with the witness on this. You think you can take him still further, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it is probably clear to you from the testimony of this witness how many times he mentioned the name of Ljubisa Vukasinovic as the person who was the most senior person there. I am repeating the question because I simply think that he's evading to answer that question, which is very simple. Mr. Vasic asked that about the commander. I'm asking him now: If that person comes from the superior command, would he be more senior by post than he is?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So is Vukasinovic more senior? I don't want to keep on with this subject, but by position is he more senior than Colonel Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time I was not in the hangar. I was there for a very short time. I could not take away his functions just because I was a lieutenant-colonel. He had received an assignment, and he knows whom he received it from, and he was carrying it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vojnovic, if the hangar is in the area of responsibility of your brigade, the Ovcara zone, could you have thrown Ljubisa Vukasinovic out? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If somebody, without being called to do so, comes to your area of responsibility from whatever command, is it not your duty to call your superior commander to say who is it that's arriving, who is -- who has come? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Secondly, he was obliged to stop and to ask whether he could enter the area of responsibility. He had to have an order to be able to enter the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it not your duty to ask him if he had an order and to introduce himself to you; and if he refused to do that, then you would need to call your own commander. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He entered the area of responsibility using his position and the position of the superior command without any permission at all. I said that yesterday. Anyone who enters the area of responsibility without the knowledge takes upon himself the risk for all that happens in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And whose function is it to protect the area of responsibility if anyone can enter without the knowledge of the person who is responsible for guarding that area of responsibility? Let's ask that.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know how it is: While combat operations are being carried out the area of responsibility is known. He wouldn't have entered had combat operations been going on. This was a peaceful time, movement was free. All he needed to do was to stop and say: All right. We're coming in to do this and this.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you kindly slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You gave us that example with somebody's front yard and a bomb being chucked into somebody's front yard.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Anybody could just walk by and you don't know who they are.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They just throw the bomb over the wall, and you say, well, it's not the fault of the person who threw the bomb but of the person on the other side of the wall who failed to catch it in time and throw it back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on. It's up to the Court to judge both my questions and your answers. You, I mean in the hangar, or having come out in front of the hangar, asked to your command to send some help and some security people.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this must be the umpteenth time I'm saying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That was perfectly in keeping with your own powers. And when this command was obeyed and when Vukic, as you say, and the soldiers came, you returned to the command and you went to Mrksic's headquarters. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Fine. So you say you heard in Vukic's testimony or that jogged your memory because Vukasinovic allegedly told him and that he then returned to the command. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have heard evidence before this honourable Trial Chamber - I will remind my friends, on page 8676 and on page 8686, dated the 11th of May - that the two of them in fact returned together that evening with Dragi Vukosavljevic and Vezmarovic. When all of them were withdrawing pursuant to your order that Vukosavljevic then conveyed or on the order of Karanfilov, we can discuss that. But we've heard testimony before this Court, we've heard evidence that Vukic did not leave right away, as you claim, after talking to Vukosavljevic [as interpreted] but he stayed there until the end. That's what we've heard here. Would you leave that possibility open?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't commit on either of these. Maybe he didn't stay for too long, but then --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness trailed off and we didn't hear him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read what I saw and what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Page 95, line 6, my question: "After talking to Vukasinovic ..." and it says "Vukosavljevic." I will now repeat, I mean this question, because your answer was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Hold on a minute, sir, Mr. Vojnovic. We have so many problems with all these surnames that all sound alike. We've heard evidence before this Trial Chamber that they returned together, when everybody was withdrawing, including Vezmarovic's entire unit stayed all the way until the end. Do you remember this as a possibility, that this is what they told you or that this is what you heard later on at the command?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't commit on this 100 per cent. I know we did talk later on and I heard the next day what Vezmarovic had told me, who had ordered him to withdraw his troops from there. If he stayed there until the end with him, Vukic or whoever you mentioned, Vukosavljevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I don't know if they were both with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've heard before this Court from a witness who is a first-hand witness, if I may call him that, who says that he drove back together from Ovcara with Vukic, with Dacic, with Vezmarovic, and the military police, that they all came together once the hangar had been vacated.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So what's the problem? They may have gone together for all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, there is an enormous problem, but that is up to some other people to judge. My position is Vukic did not exchange a single word with Vukasinovic. My position is Vukasinovic spent a very brief time outside the hangar and then left. That is my position. That is why I have confronted you with evidence that we heard in this courtroom that Vukic stayed until the end, that he stayed on until the end. That's what I'm telling you. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you that I saw Vukasinovic there. I'm telling you that Vukic spoke to him, that he was given an assignment, and what Vukasinovic responded to him. As for how long Vukasinovic stayed there, that is not something I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But about Vukic addressing him and what Vukasinovic responded to Vukic, this wasn't something you actually saw because you had left already. You heard this from Vukic later on. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Vukic told you that he had left immediately, that he had left the hangar immediately. You have been saying this for a couple of days here, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD VOJNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
